figures.finding: The Marshall Islands tax wages and salaries at 8% on the first US$10,400 a year and 12% above (Income Tax Act 1989 as amended by P.L. 2026-68, passed 16 March 2026); US contractor personnel pay 5%.
figures.applies: Wages and salaries from 2026. A tax-free first band of US$8,320 reported by payroll sites is not confirmed by a primary source and is not applied.

sources.said: impose a general 8 percent individual income tax rate on the first US$10,400 of employee wages and salaries, prorated at US$200 weekly or approximately US$867 monthly, and increased 12 percent on the amount exceeding US$10,400
impose a 5 percent individual income tax rate on U.S. contractor personnel wages and salaries
For the purposes of taxation, both levels of government treat non- citizen investments and workers the same as their citizen counterparts.

figures.finding: A worker pays 8% of covered earnings to Social Security and the employer another 8% (since 6 March 2017), the employer deducting the worker's share; a self-employed person pays both shares, on deemed earnings (75% of quarterly gross revenue where he has no workers); worker and employer each also pay 3.5% of wages to the Health Fund; covered earnings appear capped at US$10,000 a quarter.

figures.finding: A national consumption tax of 12% applies to supplies and imports from 1 October 2026; a supplier must register when taxable supplies in 12 months reach $300,000; before that date there was no national VAT, local governments levy their own sales taxes, and businesses pay the national gross revenue tax.
figures.applies: Supplies on or after 1 October 2026 (Consumption Tax Act 2025 s. 959); whether the gross revenue tax continues beside it was not read.

figures.finding: The employer deducts and withholds the wage tax as wages are paid and pays it with a return every four weeks (13 times a year), within two weeks after each period; an individual paid by an employer with no place of business or agent in the Republic (or by the United States) files and pays himself; a business pays gross revenue tax of $80 a year on the first $10,000 of gross revenue and 3% above, quarterly by 30 April, 31 July, 31 October and 31 January.
figures.applies: Income Tax Act 1989 as consolidated; whether P.L. 2026-68 or the Tax Administration Act 2025 changed these dates was not read.
